passages.text: The LORD answered Moses, “See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses in Egypt.
The LORD said to Moses, “I am the LORD.”
The LORD gave Moses authority over Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
The LORD made Moses like God to Pharaoh.
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
The LORD made Aaron Moses’ prophet.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה רְאֵ֛ה נְתַתִּ֥יךָ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִ֖יךָ יִהְיֶ֥ה נְבִיאֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You are to speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses commands.
Moses must speak everything God commands him.
Aaron is Moses’ brother.
Aaron will speak to Pharaoh.
Aaron will tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites leave his land.
passages.original: אַתָּ֣ה תְדַבֵּ֔ר אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲצַוֶּ֑ךָּ וְאַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֙יךָ֙ יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְשִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and though I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay My hand on Egypt, and by mighty acts of judgment I will bring the divisions of My people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God said He would harden Pharaoh’s heart.
God said He would do many signs in Egypt.
God said He would do many wonders in Egypt.
Pharaoh would not listen to Moses and Aaron.
God would stretch out His hand against Egypt.
God would bring His people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.
God would do this with great acts of judgment.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֥י אַקְשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֧י אֶת־ אֹתֹתַ֛י וְאֶת־ מוֹפְתַ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ וְלֹֽא־ יִשְׁמַ֤ע אֲלֵכֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־ יָדִ֖י בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוֹצֵאתִ֨י אֶת־ צִבְאֹתַ֜י אֶת־ עַמִּ֤י בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בִּשְׁפָטִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃

passages.text: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God will act with power against Egypt.
God will stretch out His hand over Egypt.
God will bring the Israelites out from among the Egyptians.
The Egyptians will know that God is the LORD when He does this.
passages.original: וְיָדְע֤וּ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בִּנְטֹתִ֥י אֶת־ יָדִ֖י עַל־ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוֹצֵאתִ֥י אֶת־ בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִתּוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet of God.
Aaron was his brother and helper.
The LORD gave Moses and Aaron commands.
Moses and Aaron obeyed the LORD.
They did exactly what the LORD told them to do.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹתָ֖ם כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃

passages.text: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
passages.sermon: Moses was eighty years old.\r\nAaron was eighty-three years old.\r\nMoses and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh.
passages.original: וּמֹשֶׁה֙ בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַֽהֲרֹ֔ן בֶּן־ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ וּשְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּדַבְּרָ֖ם אֶל־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃פ

passages.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “When Pharaoh tells you, ‘Perform a miracle,’ you are to say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,’ and it will become a serpent.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
He gave them instructions.
He said Pharaoh would speak to them.
Pharaoh would say, “Perform a miracle.”
The LORD told Moses what to say to Aaron.
Moses must tell Aaron, “Take your staff.”
Aaron must throw his staff down before Pharaoh.
The staff will become a serpent.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃ כִּי֩ יְדַבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵכֶ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנ֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם מוֹפֵ֑ת וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֧ח אֶֽת־ מַטְּךָ֛ וְהַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ לִפְנֵֽי־ פַרְעֹ֖ה יְהִ֥י לְתַנִּֽין׃

passages.text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet of God.
Aaron was his brother and helper.
The LORD gave them commands.
Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh.
They obeyed the LORD’s instructions.
Aaron took his staff.
Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh.
Aaron also threw it down in front of Pharaoh’s officials.
The staff became a serpent.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֣עַשׂוּ כֵ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־ מַטֵּ֗הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיְהִ֥י לְתַנִּֽין׃

passages.text: But Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers and magicians of Egypt, and they also did the same things by their magic arts.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh called for his wise men.
Pharaoh called for his sorcerers.
Pharaoh called for the magicians of Egypt.
The magicians of Egypt used their secret arts.
The magicians did the same things as Aaron did.
They used their magic to copy the miracle.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא֙ גַּם־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה לַֽחֲכָמִ֖ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֨וּ גַם־ הֵ֜ם חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.
passages.sermon:
The magicians of Egypt stood before Pharaoh.
Each magician held a staff.
Each magician threw his staff to the ground.
Each staff became a serpent.
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
Aaron also had a staff.
Aaron’s staff had become a serpent.
Aaron’s staff swallowed all the other staffs.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁלִ֙יכוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מַטֵּ֔הוּ וַיִּהְי֖וּ לְתַנִּינִ֑ם וַיִּבְלַ֥ע מַטֵּֽה־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֶת־ מַטֹּתָֽם׃

passages.text: Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh’s heart became hard.
Pharaoh did not listen to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD had said this would happen.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to Moses.\r\nThe LORD said Pharaoh’s heart is hard.\r\nPharaoh refuses to let the people go.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כָּבֵ֖ד לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה מֵאֵ֖ן לְשַׁלַּ֥ח הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as you see him walking out to the water. Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.
passages.sermon:
Moses was God's chosen messenger.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command.
God said, "Go to Pharaoh in the morning."
Pharaoh will go out to the water.
Stand on the bank of the Nile.
Wait there to meet Pharaoh.
Take the staff in your hand.
This staff turned into a snake before.
Hold this staff as you meet Pharaoh.
passages.original: לֵ֣ךְ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֞ה בַּבֹּ֗קֶר הִנֵּה֙ יֹצֵ֣א הַמַּ֔יְמָה וְנִצַּבְתָּ֥ לִקְרָאת֖וֹ עַל־ שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְאֹ֑ר וְהַמַּטֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְנָחָ֖שׁ תִּקַּ֥ח בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Then say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let My people go, so that they may worship Me in the wilderness. But you have not listened until now.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD sent me to you.
The LORD gave me a message for you.
The LORD says, "Let My people go."
The LORD wants His people to worship Him in the wilderness.
You have not listened to the LORD until now.
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָעִבְרִים֙ שְׁלָחַ֤נִי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י וְיַֽעַבְדֻ֖נִי בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹא־ שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ עַד־ כֹּֽה׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Behold, with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says, “By this you will know that I am the LORD.”
I hold a staff in my hand.
I will strike the water of the Nile with this staff.
The water in the Nile will turn to blood.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּזֹ֣את תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַכֶּ֣ה׀ בַּמַּטֶּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־ בְּיָדִ֗י עַל־ הַמַּ֛יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיְאֹ֖ר וְנֶהֶפְכ֥וּ לְדָֽם׃

passages.text: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God sent Moses to speak to Pharaoh.
God gave Moses a message for Pharaoh.
God said He would strike the Nile River.
The fish in the Nile will die.
The river will smell very bad.
The Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the Nile.
passages.original: וְהַדָּגָ֧ה אֲשֶׁר־ בַּיְאֹ֛ר תָּמ֖וּת וּבָאַ֣שׁ הַיְאֹ֑ר וְנִלְא֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם מִן־ הַיְאֹֽר׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers and canals and ponds and reservoirs—that they may become blood.’ There will be blood throughout the land of Egypt, even in the vessels of wood and stone.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron.
Aaron is Moses’ brother.
The LORD said, “Tell Aaron to take his staff.”
The LORD said, “Tell Aaron to stretch out his hand over the waters of Egypt.”
The waters of Egypt include their rivers.
The waters of Egypt include their canals.
The waters of Egypt include their ponds.
The waters of Egypt include all their reservoirs.”
The LORD said, “The waters will become blood.”
The LORD said, “There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt.”
The LORD said, “There will be blood even in vessels of wood.”
The LORD said, “There will be blood even in vessels of stone.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֡ן קַ֣ח מַטְּךָ֣ וּנְטֵֽה־ יָדְךָ֩ עַל־ מֵימֵ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם עַֽל־ נַהֲרֹתָ֣ם׀ עַל־ יְאֹרֵיהֶ֣ם וְעַל־ אַגְמֵיהֶ֗ם וְעַ֛ל כָּל־ מִקְוֵ֥ה מֵימֵיהֶ֖ם וְיִֽהְיוּ־ דָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה דָם֙ בְּכָל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָעֵצִ֖ים וּבָאֲבָנִֽים׃

passages.text: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded; in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was turned to blood.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron obeyed the LORD.
The LORD had given them a command.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh’s officials stood with him.
Aaron took his staff.
Aaron raised his staff.
Aaron struck the water of the Nile River.
Pharaoh and his officials watched Aaron.
All the water in the Nile River turned to blood.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵן֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֤רֶם בַּמַּטֶּה֙ וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־ הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּיְאֹ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּהָֽפְכ֛וּ כָּל־ הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר־ בַּיְאֹ֖ר לְדָֽם׃

passages.text: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. And there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God sent a plague on Egypt.
God turned the water of the Nile into blood.
All the fish in the Nile died.
The river began to stink.
The Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile.
Blood was everywhere in the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וְהַדָּגָ֨ה אֲשֶׁר־ בַּיְאֹ֥ר מֵ֙תָה֙ וַיִּבְאַ֣שׁ הַיְאֹ֔ר וְלֹא־ יָכְל֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם מִן־ הַיְאֹ֑ר וַיְהִ֥י הַדָּ֖ם בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But the magicians of Egypt did the same things by their magic arts. So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
passages.sermon:
The magicians of Egypt used their secret arts.
They did the same things Moses and Aaron did.
Pharaoh saw this.
Pharaoh’s heart became hard.
Pharaoh did not listen to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD had said this would happen.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־ כֵ֛ן חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב־ פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹא־ שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Instead, Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and did not take any of this to heart.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh saw what happened.
Pharaoh turned away.
Pharaoh went into his palace.
Pharaoh did not care about what happened.
Pharaoh did not let these things touch his heart.
passages.original: וַיִּ֣פֶן פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וְלֹא־ שָׁ֥ת לִבּ֖וֹ גַּם־ לָזֹֽאת׃

passages.text: So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.
passages.sermon:
All the Egyptians needed water to drink.
They could not drink the water from the Nile River.
So the Egyptians dug around the Nile.
They dug to find water to drink.
passages.original: וַיַּחְפְּר֧וּ כָל־ מִצְרַ֛יִם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הַיְאֹ֖ר מַ֣יִם לִשְׁתּ֑וֹת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לִשְׁתֹּ֔ת מִמֵּימֵ֖י הַיְאֹֽר׃

passages.text: And seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.
passages.sermon:
The LORD struck the Nile.
Seven days passed after this.
The seven days were complete.
passages.original: וַיִּמָּלֵ֖א שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הַכּוֹת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ הַיְאֹֽר׃פ
